Description:en: Additions and updates at the time of assessment. If the patient is on a ventilator or NIV, document that on the ventilator flowsheet as well.
Day shift or night shift column from the nursing assessment.
Temperature at the time of assessment.
Blood pressure at the time of assessment.
Heart rate at the time of assessment.
Respiratory rate at the time of assessment.
Oxygen saturation at the time of assessment.
Airway is an endotracheal tube or tracheostomy.
Oral or nasal airway is in place.
Nasal cannula, simple face mask, non-rebreather, high-flow nasal cannula, or NIV.
Cyanosis of the oral mucosa, circumoral skin, or nail beds.
Breathing effort: comfortable, labored, or retractions.
Left upper lobe lung sounds. Tick every sound that applies.
Left lower lobe lung sounds. Tick every sound that applies.
Right upper lobe lung sounds. Tick every sound that applies.
Right lower lobe lung sounds. Tick every sound that applies.
Secretion amount: none, small, moderate, or large.
Secretion color. More than one may be selected.
Orientation score written after Oriented x.
Glasgow Coma Scale eyes. 4 open, 3 voice, 2 pain, 1 none.
Glasgow Coma Scale verbal. 5 oriented, 4 confused, 3 inappropriate, 2 sounds, 1 none.
Glasgow Coma Scale motor. 6 obeys, 5 localizes, 4 withdraws, 3 flexion, 2 extension, 1 none.
Glasgow Coma Scale total, eyes plus verbal plus motor, shown over 15.
Bowel sounds normal, diarrhea, or constipation.
When the last stool was passed.
NG or OG tube length at the exit site, in centimetres.
Tube feeding is given as a bolus.
Reason the urinary catheter is still needed.
Urine appearance. More than one may be selected.
Skin, mucosa, and musculoskeletal system are intact.
Skin, mucosa, or musculoskeletal system is not intact.
Description of rashes, wounds, pressure injury and stage, dressings, drains, and locations.
Capillary refill less than 3 seconds or greater than 3 seconds.
Vital signs at the time of assessment, including airway, breathing, disability, GCS, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, skin, and IV sites.
Cardiovascular and circulatory assessment: rhythm, capillary refill, pulses, and edema.
